That glow around the bee and the butterfly is doing something lovely - the subjects stay sharp while everything around them goes soft and lit. How did you get the glow to sit like that - mostly the new feature, or a lot of masking by hand?

answers.author: janirube
answers.text: thank you so much ✨ the main part is masking 😁

replies.text: The mist does half the work here - those orange beeches fading into the fog while the leaf-covered floor glows underneath. Was the fog already in the trees when you arrived, or did it roll in while you were shooting?

That chandelier glowing against the stone wall is the whole frame - and then the lone figure on the stairs walks right into it. Was the light the reason you stopped, or the figure? The Track 30 sign is the perfect pin to Grand Central.

answers.author: zane_claytor
answers.text: Thank you. I appreciate that. It was definitely the chandelier and the angle of the staircase. That brought me to compose there. I just had to wait for the right person with a darker contrast coming down the stairs.

replies.text: A dahlia on pure black - the pink spikes read like fireworks and the yellow center holds the middle. I think isolating it against nothing was the right call. What made you pick this one to open the flora call?

answers.author: jenkophotos
answers.text: Thanks for the comment and feedback! I just think it's a striking flower in general, it really pops.

replies.text: What are you hoping the entries bring that this one doesn't? Those curves are a strong opener - the white ramp winding up out of frame, the grid walkway cutting across it, and black-and-white doing all the work.

answers.author: pattykl
answers.text: I share mine and everyone shares theirs and we all get enlightened  by beauty!!✨✨🥰

replies.text: That mooring ring in the foreground does all the anchoring - wet stone, waves washing the pier, and the boats sitting under a dark sky behind it. Where is this harbor?

Same cow, same lens, and the fog still changes everything - that white background in slide one turns her face into a portrait, and the dark ears do all the framing. Which day did she hold still longer for, the foggy one or the clear one?

answers.author: tanya_kreil
answers.text: Hard to say.  I forget.  I'm more concerned about them moving their ears.

replies.text: The window frame on the right is what makes this one - the murmuration gets the whole orange sky, and then the glass doubles it on the edge like a second sunset. How long did the flock keep swirling over the pier before it settled?
